stories.headline: DeepSeek ships experimental multimodal V4-Flash-Vision, claims agent scores near Anthropic's Opus 4.8

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek put DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp live on its API platform on August 21, 2026, an experimental multimodal model callable with model='deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp'
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp is now live on the DeepSeek API Platform! This experimental multimodal model matches DeepSeek-V4-Flash on text capabilities—including agents, reasoning, and world knowledge.

key_facts.fact: On agent benchmarks that require visual understanding, DeepSeek says the model makes a major leap over the text-only V4-Flash, bringing multimodal agent performance close to Opus-4.8
key_facts.excerpt: On agent benchmarks that require visual understanding, DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Vision-Exp delivers a significant leap over DeepSeek-V4-Flash, bringing its multimodal agent capabilities close to Opus-4.8.

key_facts.fact: On DeepSeek's own published table the model beats Opus-4.8 on three of eleven benchmarks; it scores 36.5 vs V4-Flash's 26.2 on ApexBench and 27.3 vs 25.2 on Agents' Last Exam
key_facts.excerpt: On DeepSeek's own published table, it beats that model on three benchmarks out of eleven. ... On ApexBench that is 36.5 against 26.2, and on Agents' Last Exam 27.3 against 25.2.

key_facts.fact: DeepSeek's own footnote concedes the comparison is skewed: on those two evaluations the text-only V4-Flash 'ignores multimodal elements contained therein', i.e. it is scored on tests with images it cannot see
key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek's own footnote explains part of the gap. In those two evaluations, it says, the text-based V4-Flash "ignores multimodal elements contained therein". The older model is being scored on tests containing images it cannot see.

key_facts.fact: The model is a sparse mixture-of-experts with 13B active parameters out of 284B total, a 1,048,576-token context window, and on OpenRouter costs $0.22 per million input tokens and $0.66 per million output tokens
key_facts.excerpt: It is a sparse mixture-of-experts model with 13B active parameters out of 284B total. ... It has a 1,048,576-token context window and a maximum output of 384,000 tokens. ... costs $0.22/M input tokens and $0.66/M output tokens

key_facts.fact: Images are billed as tokens, up to 384 tokens each at V4-Flash pricing, and DeepSeek shipped Harness 0.1.1 the same day with out-of-the-box support
key_facts.excerpt: Images are tokenized for billing: up to 384 tokens each, at V4-Flash pricing ... DeepSeek Harness 0.1.1 was released today with out-of-the-box support for the new model.

stories.headline: Anthropic expects to match or beat SpaceX's record IPO, may file publicly by end of August

key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic PBC expects to match or beat the size of SpaceX's record-setting initial public offering, according to people familiar with the matter... The Claude developer is running the numbers as it prepares to file publicly for its potential mega-IPO as soon as the end of this month

key_facts.fact: Recent investor briefings led by CFO Krishna Rao skirted the question of valuation
key_facts.excerpt: Recent investor briefings led by Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao skirted the question of valuation, they said.

key_facts.fact: SpaceX raised $75 billion at the outset in the biggest first-time share sale ever, rising to $86.2 billion once the overallotment option was exercised
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk's rocket and satellite firm raised $75 billion at the outset, making it the biggest first-time share sale ever... The final figure increased to $86.2 billion with the so-called overallotment option

key_facts.fact: A first-time share sale topping SpaceX would make 2026 the best year on record for US IPO volume; new listings have raised $160.6 billion through August 19 versus 2021's $195.2 billion high

stories.headline: Nvidia pays Poolside $6B to license its 'Model Factory', invests $1B and hires 109 staff

key_facts.fact: Poolside struck a non-exclusive licensing deal with Nvidia worth $6 billion plus a $1 billion investment at a $12 billion pre-money valuation, per an investor letter obtained by Newcomer
key_facts.excerpt: Poolside AI, the artificial intelligence model-building startup, has struck a non-exclusive licensing deal with Nvidia for $6 billion, plus a $1 billion investment in Poolside at a $12 billion pre-money valuation, according to a letter to investors obtained by Newcomer.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia is licensing the 'Model Factory' — the system Poolside used to build its Laguna model — and is extending job offers to 109 Poolside employees who worked on it; the three founders stay
key_facts.excerpt: The employees worked on the Laguna model and are getting job offers from Nvidia. Nvidia is licensing the 'Model Factory,' the system Poolside used to build its model... On top of that, Nvidia is investing $1 billion at a $12 billion pre-money valuation. The three founders are staying on.

key_facts.fact: The investor letter insists the transaction is 'not an acquisition and it is not an acquihire'; Poolside plans to distribute the $6 billion to its investors by the end of next year
key_facts.excerpt: is "not an acquisition and it is not an acquihire," the [letter] says... Poolside plans to distribute the $6 billion to its investors by the end of next year.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia has used the same structure before, with deals for Groq ($20 billion) and Enfabrica ($900 million)
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia struck similar deals with Groq($20 billion) and Enfabrica($900 million).

key_facts.fact: The license is non-exclusive, so Poolside can keep selling the technology; the platform produces generative AI models tailored to software development
key_facts.excerpt: The $6 billion licensing deal is non-exclusive, meaning Poolside can still sell its technology to other buyers. What Nvidia gets is access to Poolside's 'Model Factory,' the startup's platform for producing generative AI models tailored to software development.

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported in July that Nvidia was weighing an investment of up to $1 billion in Poolside, which was seeking $2 billion at a $12 billion valuation after being worth $3 billion a year earlier
key_facts.excerpt: Poolside is seeking to raise some $2bn at a $12bn valuation, and has thus far secured $1bn in commitments for the round... Poolside raising funds at $12bn is a significant jump from the valuation of $3bn just last year.

stories.headline: Google's open Gemma models pass 1 billion downloads and 100,000 community variants

key_facts.fact: Google said on August 20, 2026 that the Gemma family of open models has surpassed one billion cumulative downloads
key_facts.excerpt: When we introduced Gemma, our goal was simple: empower developers to build responsible, innovative AI applications anywhere... Today, the Gemma family has surpassed a billion downloads.

key_facts.fact: Over the past two years developers have published more than 100,000 Gemma variants, an ecosystem Google calls the 'Gemmaverse'
key_facts.excerpt: Over the past two years, developers have published over one-hundred thousand Gemma model variants and built a thriving ecosystem of innovation we call the Gemmaverse.

key_facts.fact: Google is launching an 'Awesome Gemma' repository on GitHub as an official directory of community projects, fine-tunes and tools
key_facts.excerpt: That's why we are launching the Awesome Gemma repository on GitHub.

key_facts.fact: It is the first time Google has put a cumulative total on Gemma adoption since the family launched in early 2024; the announcement came from DeepMind VP Clement Farabet and product director Olivier Lacombe
key_facts.excerpt: The figures, disclosed in Google's official announcement by Clement Farabet, a vice president at Google DeepMind, and product director Olivier Lacombe, mark the first time Google has put a cumulative total on Gemma adoption since the family launched in early 2024.

key_facts.fact: Google's recent Gemma Challenge on Kaggle drew more than 1,600 project submissions, with winners to be announced in the coming weeks
key_facts.excerpt: The company also noted that its recent Gemma Challenge on Kaggle drew more than 1,600 project submissions, with winners to be announced in the coming weeks.

key_facts.fact: At the Gemma 4 launch in April 2026 the cumulative download figure was 400 million, meaning downloads more than doubled in about four months
key_facts.excerpt: since the launch of our first generation, developers have downloaded Gemma over 400 million times, building a vibrant Gemmaverse of more than 100,000 variants

stories.headline: OpenAI gives ChatGPT on Mac access to iMessage, SMS and RCS — reading, drafting and sending texts

key_facts.fact: OpenAI added an Apple Messages plugin to the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS that reads and searches chats and prepares and sends messages, working with iMessage, SMS and RCS
key_facts.excerpt: The new Apple Messages plugin lets ChatGPT read and search chats on a Mac, and prepare and send messages. OpenAI says it is available across all plans in the ChatGPT desktop app for macOS, with support in both ChatGPT Work and Codex.

key_facts.fact: The plugin works only in ChatGPT Work and Codex, not in regular ChatGPT chats, and for now only on Apple silicon Macs, not Intel machines
key_facts.excerpt: It doesn't let you interact with ChatGPT remotely through Messages, and it doesn't work in regular ChatGPT chats. ... For now, the feature only works with ChatGPT on Apple silicon Macs and not Intel machines.

key_facts.fact: Users can ask ChatGPT to delete messages, draft and send messages on their behalf, or search information buried in message history
key_facts.excerpt: You can also ask ChatGPT to delete messages for you, draft and send messages on your behalf, or search for information buried deep in your message history.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI told Bloomberg the plugin runs locally on the user's machine and 'doesn't create an index of all someone's messages'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI told Bloomberg that the plug-in runs locally on a user's machine and that it "doesn't create an index of all someone's messages."

key_facts.fact: Sending is approval-gated by default; OpenAI warns that persistent approval 'removes your final chance to review a message before ChatGPT sends it as you'
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI encourages users to keep an eye on what ChatGPT is doing and discourages turning on persistent approval, warning that doing so "removes your final chance to review a message before ChatGPT sends it as you"

key_facts.fact: Administrators in managed workspaces can disable the plugin via the existing Computer Use control; the same update added unified pinned threads across desktop and iOS and read-only Codex thread snapshots
key_facts.excerpt: In managed workspaces, administrators can disable the Apple Messages plugin through the existing Computer Use control. Beyond Messages, the update also brings unified pinned threads across the ChatGPT desktop app and iOS, along with read-only Codex thread snapshots.
